title: Regional affinity and compliance spillover controls for dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers running Dedicated pools across multiple zones and regions need strong placement control so that traffic remains within contracted geographies while also meeting throughput guarantees. Current behavior permits aggressive cross-zone spillover under autoscale pressure which violates some data residency contracts and causes unpredictable tail latency.

Goal: Implement a policy-driven placement layer that enforces ordered affinity preferences, soft spillover gates, and compliance locks. The policy should allow: (1) deterministic preferred-zone routing, (2) configurable soft-fallback windows for autoscale events, and (3) hard-residency enforcement for contracts that require regional-only placement. The system must maintain throughput SLOs where possible and offer clear observability when spillover or rejects occur.

High-level approach and trade-offs:
- Affinity graph: represent region/zone preference as weighted affinities. This allows incremental preference changes without binary on/off decisions. Trade-off: increased scheduler complexity vs finer control and smoother failover.
- Soft spillover window: when local capacity is saturated, allow spillover to adjacent zones for a short, configurable grace window before rejecting or throttling. Trade-off: briefly violates strict residency but maintains availability and throughput. For customers with legal constraints we will allow a "residency lock" flag to disable spillover.
- Priority lanes: reserve throughput lanes (tokens) per region for guaranteed capacity. This satisfies committed throughput SLAs but increases capacity fragmentation; we will make reserve sizes adaptive based on recent utilization to limit wasted capacity.
- Autoscale policy integration: reconcile existing autoscaler decisions with placement gates so scale-out attempts prefer local capacity first, then expand to reserved lanes, then soft-spill, then fallback models.

Acceptance criteria:
- New policy language and API to declare preferred_zones, spillover_window_seconds, residency_lock (boolean), and reserved_throughput_pct.
- E2E tests that verify: strict residency_lock blocks cross-region allocation; soft_spill allows temporary cross-zone allocation and reverts within window; reserved_throughput enforces minimum available QPS under background load.
- Observability: per-request tagging indicating placement decision (preferred|reserved|spillover|blocked) and a dashboard showing spillover rates, blocked allocations, and reserved lane utilization.
- No regression in median latency; P95 tail must not increase by >5% under synthetic workload used in benchmarks.

Design docs and artifacts:
- Design brief: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Regional+Affinity+and+Spillover+Controls (draft)
- Scheduler prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/1458 (WIP)
- Autoscaler integration branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscale/compare/feature/placement-gates (draft)
- Benchmark dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/throughput/placement-policy-experiments

Rollout plan:
1) Merge placement policy API + opt-in config flags behind feature flag gate (runtime-config:placement-policy). Limit to internal dogfood orgs.
2) Run synthetic soak for 72h with controlled network partitions to exercise soft spill and reserved lanes. Monitor dashboard alerts and SLO impact.
3) Gradually enable for select customers with contractual residency flexibility. Collect feedback and tune defaults (spillover_window_seconds default = 60s).
4) Add enforcement mode for customers who opt for legal residency_lock. Contractual onboarding with clear guidance on throughput limits during full-region outages.

Open questions:
- Default sizing heuristic for reserved_throughput_pct: absolute percent vs workload-driven baseline? Proposed: baseline percentile of 95th on recent 24h traffic with floor of 5%.
- How should we bill reserved lanes when adaptive reserves are used? (Accounting required between Dedicated commitments and observed reserved utilization.)

Next steps: finalize API schema, complete scheduler prototype tests, and coordinate with Console team for dashboard widgets and rollout controls.
